topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the lecture objectives, and sets the stage for examining the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic versus Extrinsic Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, focusing on the interplay between intrinsic random mutational processes and extrinsic environmental risk factors.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, illustrated through the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific chemical and physical agents undergo metabolic activation to form DNA adducts and induce genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how non-mutagenic tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host developmental timing provide permissive conditions for tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental risk versus benefit considerations.
